# Completeness & notation keys (IPCC 2006 Vol 1 Ch 8)

Coverage of every AFOLU source/sink category, plus the energy categories that border it - residential, which receives AFOLU's one cross-sector transfer, and the transport modes outside 1.A.3.b - with the IPCC notation key and the reason. **E** estimated, **NE** not estimated (known gap), **NO** not occurring, **IE** included elsewhere, **NA** not applicable.

Summary: E 54 &middot; NE 71 &middot; NO 4 &middot; IE 8 &middot; NA 1

Why the NE rows are NE, from `data/data_gaps.csv`: no-data-exists 5 &middot; not-acquired 93 &middot; not-archived 23 &middot; not-extracted 14 &middot; not-reconciled 32 &middot; paid-access 1. Only `no-data-exists` means the datum has never been measured; the rest are documents not yet obtained, parsed or reconciled.

Pakistan Railways Year Book metered fuel consumption x IPCC Vol 2 Ch 3 Table 3.4.1, the RAIL table - its N2O factor is \\num{7.3} times the road value. Railway diesel is its own OCAC customer-class row, outside the road control by the source's structure, and the Year Book figure serves as an independent cross-check on that row (3.8 percent apart at the matched year) rather than a deduction. The mainline network has been diesel-only since about 2010 (electric energy NIL from the 2010-2015 quinquennium in the Year Book's own historical table), so there is no scope-2 stream in the inventory years; urban electric rail (Lahore Orange Line) is outside the operator, has zero direct 1A3c combustion, and its electricity is accounted under power. AP-42 factors on the sector's own fuel give roughly 399 kt SO2, 183 kt NOx and 664 kt filterable PM UNCONTROLLED - what leaves the furnace. Pakistan's coal units carry precipitators and the newer ones desulphurisation, and no national dataset records which is fitted where or how it performs, so the controlled figure is the row below. The earlier note here said this was blocked on EMEP/EEA factors; re-deriving from AP-42 showed that was the wrong diagnosis - what was missing was never the factors but the FUEL ANALYSIS, which NEPRA does not publish. Sulfur and ash are carried as published ranges with the uncertainty read off them, as the fugitives sector does. SPLIT BY COAL RANK since August 2026: 79 percent of coal energy is Thar lignite on AP-42 Section 1.7's own factors (30S, 6.5A, its own size distribution) and lignite's 11.9 TJ/Gg NCV, the rest imported bituminous on Section 1.1 (38S, 10A) - the rank split RAISED the bound roughly by half, because a tonne of lignite carries half the energy so the sulfur- and ash-scaled factors nearly double per TJ. Grid bagasse cogeneration is estimated from Section 1.8 (PM and NOx; the section publishes no SOx or CO factor). Grid gas NOx blends the boiler and turbine chapters by the plant ledger's heat-rate classification (80 percent turbine), with the 6 percent unresolved share kept on the boiler factor and reported. |

Applying a removal rate without it would be inventing the number that matters most, since it spans an order of magnitude between uncontrolled and well-controlled. |

_The Agriculture sector (3.A-3.H) is complete for all occurring categories; the notation-key gaps (NE) are the Tier-1 simplifications (FSOM, cropland/grassland SOC, HWP) that need land-use-change or field data. Dung-cake combustion is the one cross-sector transfer, and it is now closed at both ends: the nitrogen leaves Manure Management (IE) and arrives in 1.A.4.b (`pkinv.sectors.residential`), where the mass it implies is burnt._
